title: The Motor Seal-In (Real Field Wiring)
concept:
## Assign vs compare

Two symbols people mix up: `:=` **assigns** a value; `=` **compares** two values. Boolean operators are `AND`, `OR`, `NOT`, `XOR`.

## Reading the field devices (XIC / XIO)

A standard 3-wire motor starter wires its devices a specific way, and that wiring drives your code:

    DEVICE       CONTACT   INPUT BIT READS...
    Start_PB     N.O.      TRUE only while pressed
    Stop_PB      N.C.      TRUE when NOT pressed, FALSE when pressed
    Motor_OL     N.C.      TRUE when healthy, FALSE when tripped

Read each device the right way. **XIC** means "use the tag as-is". **XIO** means "use `NOT tag`":

- **Start_PB** is **(N.O.)** → **XIC** (as-is). TRUE only while pressed — perfect to start.
- **Stop_PB** is **(N.C.)**, wired fail-safe → **XIC** (as-is). It is TRUE while NOT pressed, so ANDing it in permits running.
- **Motor_OL** is **(N.C.)** → **XIC** (as-is). TRUE while the overload is healthy.

Because Stop and the overload are **normally closed**, their bits are already TRUE while running normally. You AND them in **exactly as they are, never inverted**:

    Motor_Run := (Start_PB OR Motor_Run) AND Stop_PB AND Motor_OL;

## Why no NOT on Stop?

Pressing the N.C. stop **opens** the circuit → `Stop_PB` goes FALSE → the whole expression goes FALSE → the motor drops out. Break the wire and the same thing happens. That is the **fail-safe**: the hardware provides the inversion so your logic does not. Writing `NOT Stop_PB` defeats it, the #1 rookie mistake. In ladder terms you examine a N.C. stop with an **XIC** contact, not XIO.

## The seal-in

The `(Start_PB OR Motor_Run)` part is the **seal-in**: once running, `Motor_Run` holds itself on, so you can release the momentary start button and the motor keeps running until Stop (or the overload) breaks the rung.
ab_note:
This is the ST version of a seal-in rung. In Studio 5000 ladder you'd examine
Stop_PB and Motor_OL with NORMAL (XIC) contacts -- NOT XIO -- precisely because
the N.C. field wiring makes the bit TRUE when safe. Using XIO (or NOT in ST) on
a N.C. stop is the classic mistake that defeats the fail-safe.
siemens_note:
Identical in SCL: :=, AND, OR are standard IEC operators, and a N.C. stop is
ANDed straight in. Siemens field points live in the PLC tag table with the same
N.O./N.C. wiring reality behind them.
task:
Given BOOL tags Start_PB (N.O.), Stop_PB (N.C.), Motor_OL (N.C.), and output
Motor_Run, write ONE assignment implementing a real 3-wire seal-in:

    - Motor_Run latches on when Start_PB is pressed and holds itself on
    - Pressing Stop_PB (N.C.) drops it out
    - An overload trip (Motor_OL goes FALSE) also drops it out

Stop_PB and Motor_OL are normally-closed -- AND them in as-is, do NOT use NOT.

(* Lesson 02 -- The Motor Seal-In (real field wiring) *)
(* Wiring key:  N.O. contact -> read AS-IS (XIC)   |   N.C. contact -> AS-IS, fail-safe (XIC)   |   NOT x = XIO *)

VAR
    Start_PB  : BOOL;   (* N.O. start PB   -> XIC (as-is): TRUE when pressed             *)
    Stop_PB   : BOOL;   (* N.C. stop PB    -> XIC (as-is): TRUE when NOT pressed (fail-safe) *)
    Motor_OL  : BOOL;   (* N.C. overload   -> XIC (as-is): TRUE when healthy             *)
    Motor_Run : BOOL;   (* motor contactor coil (output)                                *)
END_VAR

(* ----- YOUR LOGIC : write your answer between these two lines ----- *)
    (* TODO: seal-in so Motor_Run holds itself on; AND the N.C. devices in AS-IS (XIC), never inverted. *)
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)

solution:
(* Lesson 02 -- The Motor Seal-In (real field wiring) *)
(* Wiring key:  N.O. contact -> read AS-IS (XIC)   |   N.C. contact -> AS-IS, fail-safe (XIC)   |   NOT x = XIO *)

VAR
    Start_PB  : BOOL;   (* N.O. start PB   -> XIC (as-is): TRUE when pressed             *)
    Stop_PB   : BOOL;   (* N.C. stop PB    -> XIC (as-is): TRUE when NOT pressed (fail-safe) *)
    Motor_OL  : BOOL;   (* N.C. overload   -> XIC (as-is): TRUE when healthy             *)
    Motor_Run : BOOL;   (* motor contactor coil (output)                                *)
END_VAR

(* ----- YOUR LOGIC : write your answer between these two lines ----- *)
Motor_Run := (Start_PB OR Motor_Run) AND Stop_PB AND Motor_OL;
(* ------------------------------------------------------------------ *)
